Author: Ali Can

> This mini project aims to conduct a statistical descriptive analysis based on dataset "ToothGrowth"

# 0. Import

``` {r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(e1071)
  library(car)
})
```

# 1. Data Exploration and Manipulation

1. Call the dataset and see the first 6 rows

``` {r}
data(ToothGrowth)
tg <- ToothGrowth
head(tg)
```
2. See the dimensions and structure of the dataset

``` {r}
cat(dim(tg))
str(tg)
```
3. See the numerical summary of the dataset

``` {r}
summary(tg)
```
> Obviously, dataset has 3 variables.

> - "len" shows the elongation in teeth. Mean and median are close indicating normality.

> - "supp" shows the method of vitamin C intake: either by pill (VC, vitaminc C) or juice (OJ, orange juice). This is a categoric field of values (OJ, VC). There are equal unmber of records (30) for each.

> - "dose" shows the dose of intake per day. This is categoric field of values (0.5, 1, 2). Median is 1 indicating uniform distribution

4. Boxplot of "len" IAW "supp" category

``` {r}
tg |>
  ggplot(aes(y=len)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill=supp)) +
  labs(title="Teeth Length Distribution by Supplement", x="", y="Teeth Length", fill="supplement")
```

# Hypothesis Tests

### 1. Is there a considerable difference in "len" between "supp" categories: OJ, VC

``` {r}
oj_len <- tg[tg$supp=="OJ", "len"]
vc_len <- tg[tg$supp=="VC", "len"]

t.test(x=oj_len, y=vc_len)
# defaults: alt:two sided test, conf.level: 0.95, paired=F, var.equal=F
```
> Comments

Assumptions: We seek for difference. Hence two sided test is applied.

1. Calculated positive t value is less than what alpha (0.05) dictates.

2. P value is greater than alpha

3. Confidence interval includes zero

RESULT: Null hypothesis of "means are equal" is FAILED TO REJECT.

### 2. Is there a considerable difference in "len" between "dose" categories: 0.5, 1, 2

> Data manipulation

``` {r}
half_len <- tg[tg$dose==0.5, "len"]
one_len <- tg[tg$dose==1, "len"]
two_len <- tg[tg$dose==2, "len"]
```

> Fist t test between the teeth length effect of 0.5 and 1 doses of vitamin c supplement

``` {r}
t.test(x=half_len, y=one_len, alt="less")
# defaults: conf.level: 0.95, paired=F, var.equal=F
```

> Second t test between the teeth length effect of 1 and 2 doses of vitamin c supplement

``` {r}
t.test(x=one_len, y=two_len, alt="less")
# defaults: conf.level: 0.95, paired=F, var.equal=F
```
> Comments

Assumptions: We assume lesser dose would translate into lesser teeth elongation. Hence one sided (lesser than) test is applied.

1. calculated t values are considerably less than what alpha (0.05) dictates.

2. p values is way lesser than alpha

3. Confidence intervals does not include zero

RESULT: Null hypothesis of "true difference in means is NOT less than 0" is rejected.

### 3. Is there a considerable difference in "len" between "supp" categories: OJ, VC when the "dose":2

``` {r}
tg_two <- tg[tg$dose==2,]

oj_two_len <- tg[tg_two$supp=="OJ", "len"]
vc_two_len <- tg[tg_two$supp=="VC", "len"]

t.test(x=oj_two_len, y=vc_two_len)
# defaults: alt:two sided test, conf.level: 0.95, paired=F, var.equal=F)
```
> Comments

Assumptions: We seek for difference. Hence two sided test is applied.

1. calculated negative t value is considerably more than what alpha (0.05) dictates.

2. p values is way greater than alpha

3. Confidence intervals includes zero

RESULT: Null hypothesis of "true difference in means is 0" is failed to reject.
